A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAnG/RNA-BAnG work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic generation experiments and protein-conditioned RNA evaluations, including baseline comparisons, diversity and novelty results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds synthetic stress tests, component ablations, preprocessing case studies and alternative scoring analyses.

M1.justification: The described two-anchor generation procedure, attention architecture and two-stage training objective remain unchanged. Component removal and protein preprocessing appear as additional experiments, without replacing the proposed model or its standard inference procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds DualBindMix and DualBindMix Random, requiring simultaneous motifs; its DualBind row matches the existing DoubleBind task. Domain/IDR-trimmed protein scenarios are also added. Biological training sources and the main 71-sample test set remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding generation comparisons retain autoregressive generation, iterative/IAnG variants, random sampling, GenerRNA and RNAFLOW. Newly used sequence-alignment and motif-search tools serve as evaluators, without changing the generation baseline sets.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation protocols with BLASTN similarity scoring and MAFFT/MOODS motif scoring, including sigmoid transformation and a separate 0.4 haRNA threshold. Added experiments test sequence lengths of 100, 200 and uniformly sampled 40–50 tokens, motif spacing, component removal and protein preprocessing. Existing main training and test settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices B.4 and F.2–F.5 add length and motif-spacing sensitivity tests, geometric-attention and cross-attention-position ablations, protein-preprocessing case studies and alternative-scoring checks. These substantially expand analysis beyond v1's threshold sensitivity, structural-confidence and training-similarity analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F.5 newly specifies Pearson correlation to quantify agreement between DeepCLIP and motif-based scoring. Existing diversity/novelty uncertainty summaries remain unchanged, and no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values, but substantial results are added. Table B.3 reports both-motif proportions of 0.97 with fixed spacing and 0.05 with random spacing. Appendix F.5 reports motif-scoring areas of 0.49 for RNA-BAnG and 0.40 for random generation, with cross-scorer correlation 0.64. Additional results include comparator performance curves, ablations and preprocessing outcomes.

T1.justification: Equation 1 introduces separate left/right lengths and explicit conditioning contexts. Their indices are not equivalent to v1: the first left token now conditions on x1 as well as x0, although Figure 2 generates x1 later. This introduces a local inconsistency with the retained generation order. Algorithm A.1 is unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: anchored bidirectional generation, the protein-conditioned RNA-BAnG architecture and favorable synthetic and RNA-generation comparisons. The conclusion's added 'during inference' clarifies an already established scope; the new experiments support rather than redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive boundaries concerning uncertain motif spacing, domain/IDR preprocessing and homology-based scoring of designed sequences. It replaces v1's geometric-attention nonconvergence assertion with an interpretation based on measured performance differences. It also qualifies presumed dissimilarity to RNAFLOW's training data instead of asserting zero similarity.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code/model release; v2 states that code and weights are available at a specified repository. v2 also adds DeepCLIP parameter-count and checkpoint-selection details, plus reproducible MAFFT/MOODS settings and motif-construction instructions. Existing model dimensions, training budgets and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MAFFT, MOODS and position-weight-matrix background: Katoh and Standley, Korhonen et al., Stormo et al., and Schneider and Stephens. The broader positioning against existing RNA-generation methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand the generation explanation, condense tokenization details and reorganize the evaluation-protocol discussion. Appendix F gains descriptive subsections, and an Impact Statement is added. The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables B.2–B.3 and Figures F.1 and F.4–F.8 for the expanded analyses. It merges the two architecture diagrams into Figure A.1, redraws Figure 1 and relocates several displays. The original per-sample score distributions are retained as Figures G.1–G.2 rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through component ablations, alternative scoring that checks reliance on DeepCLIP, and stress tests exposing a multi-motif failure boundary. Reported code/weights availability also improves reproducibility. These gains address important evidential gaps in v1 and outweigh the localized conditioning-index inconsistency introduced in Equation 1.
